title: Thanksgiving at the shack
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thanksgiving. Not the house this year; the shack. The uncle in the chair, the smoked salmon on the counter, Gully, Wood, the dog under the counter. Nobody says grace. The uncle says 'alder' and that's it. Wood draws the four of them from the door and it's the first family portrait the strip has done.

panels.composition: The shack, Thanksgiving, the stove going, the smoked salmon on the counter on butcher paper. The UNCLE in the chair inside for once. GULLY. WOOD. BARNABY under the counter.

image.prompt: inside a warm bait shack on a holiday with smoked salmon on butcher paper on the counter, an old man in a lawn chair, a stocky teenager, a young man and a small dog beneath the counter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The salmon. The paper. Gully's knife.

an old man in a lawn chair by a stove, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: From the door: the four of them in the lamplight, the chair, the counter, the dog's tail out from under it. The strip's first family portrait. It doesn't call it that. Nobody says grace.
